questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try study exchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed it very much, but it was not my first priority of destination.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not overly complicated, but I was lucky to know somebody who was there the year before. Definitely not easy breazy:)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of good information and very helpful service once we started - but before the exchange, it was a bit more slow and complicated to get help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were lucky to find an apartment to sublet via Facebook. Join all the facebook groups and put on notifications:)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Saint Gilles and Ixelles are cozy and cool, but most areas in the city has its vibe and special cool things. And the city is not too big to get around fairly quickly anyway. Find accommodation in the south or middle part of the city to be close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you are in Brussels for less than 6 months and is an EU citizen, you can ignore the requirements about registering at the address. That makes it a bit easier to find a place.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can use the first week to go to all the courses, and you dont have to commit to courses before a while in. It is quite flexible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of help was available with the academic coordinators at ULB. They were very quick to respond and very flexible.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first I struggled to get all courses in english (my academic french is not very good) but we managed to find a way.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of the courses on BA level are in french, and as a BA student I was not allowed to do more than two Masters courses. It made it difficult to get all courses in french.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did three MA and three BA courses. The level was of course different, but I was challenged by all of them. Especially the MA courses were a bit difficult for me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only lectures and almost to interaction with students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to political science, introduction to EU politics, decision making in the EU, democratization and autocratization, globalization studies, introduction to political communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Globalization studies was the most interesting but also the most difficult one for me

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My bike got stolen, so I had to buy a new one:)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive, but very comparable to danish prices

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ULB sports was a cool thing, but a lot of the teams were either filled quickly or cancelled because of not enough participants, so I ended up only using it a couple of times, and signing up for football at a club outside uni.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot!! Both ESL and all the student activities - sports, culture, you name it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The events at Coin Culture are cool - find them on IG.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I never really left brussels, there are so many markets, exhibitions, events, bars and parties, you can go to in town in your free time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I do not speak french, and it was no problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sports or student activities - but this is easier if you speak french. Otherwise sign up for the ESL activities - there are several each week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The culture is quite french - things will start when they start and people are often late:)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and city life. Markets and people sitting outside drinking wine very late on all days of the week

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Things might seem chaotic, but the ULB staff are really nice and good at helping you - it will work out. Buy or bring a bike, I loved to have mine there. I found the academic level to be very similar to Denmark, but the exams a closed book and in hand, so I struggled a bit with them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being a part of a local football club with Belgians and expats - I had a lot of my social life there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was a bummer not speaking french - if my level was better initially I could have learned a lot more:):):)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Brussels is such a nice city!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
